title: Labeler pocket guides + micro examples
content:
Purpose: quick, chew-sized guidance for labelers when they hit low-frequency annoyances. Meant to be printed as index-cards or kept as a pinned note in the annotation UI. Not exhaustive — notes to self, will iterate after next audit.

Top-level rules (short):
- Favor consistency over perfection when unsure. Pick the most conservative label and document it.
- If you change a labeling pattern mid-batch, flag the batch and add a 1-line rationale.
- Prefer explicit token spans when the UI supports it — avoid whole-sentence heuristics unless instructed.

Heuristics (micro):
1) Abbreviations and concatenated tokens (e.g., "acctNum", "SSNmasked"):
   - If digits present and clearly an identifier -> PII label. If alpha-only but pattern implies id -> comment + possible PII review.
   - Example: "acctNum: 274-xx" -> label numeric span only.

2) Redacted/obfuscated PII: "****-1234", "[REDACTED]", "xXx-9876":
   - Treat as PII if position & surrounding text imply real value (billing, contact info).
   - If redaction ambiguous (logs, dummy data), add tag `uncertain-pii` and short note.

3) Short fragments and lists (UI often shows bullets):
   - Label the minimal token span that qualifies. For list of phones, each phone gets own span.

4) Embedded code / stack traces:
   - Do not label code-like hashes (sha256, UUID) unless the surrounding instructions indicate they are user data.
   - Example: `TRACE: 3a7f...` in an error log -> usually infrastructure id; mark with `infra-id` comment not PII.

5) Dates and relative times: "6/14/22", "Q3 2023", "yesterday 3pm":
   - Absolute calendar dates -> Date label. Relative -> not labeled unless user explicitly supplies a real timestamp. 
   - If date range implies billing cycle -> label both dates and add note `billing-context`.

6) Multilingual mixes (es+en, cyrillic fragments):
   - Label content based on semantic role, not language. PII in Spanish is still PII.
   - For ambiguous tokenization (no spaces), try to select contiguous character spans; if impossible, use whole-phrase span and note `tokenization-approx`.

7) Names vs. organizations: short ambiguous tokens ("Apple", "Jordan"):
   - If token is person-first-name-like and surrounding text contains verbs like 'said', 'phoned' -> Person.
   - If preceded by 'Inc', 'LLC', or in contact block -> Org. When ambiguous, prefer Org for business contexts, Person for chatty transcripts.

Quick decision tree (for annotator):
- Does the text look like an identifier (digits, emails, phone patterns, known PII markers)? -> Label as PII.
- Is it a hash/tech-id in logs? -> comment `infra-id` not PII unless user-context claimed.
- Mixed language or weird tokenization? -> use whole-phrase span + `tokenization-approx` tag.

Sample labeling micro-cases (examples to paste into UI):
- "Customer acctNum: 274-xx" -> span: "274-xx" ; tag: ACCOUNT_ID ; note: keep redaction suffix.
- "Llamame a las 6pm" (mixed chat) -> no PII; if phone present -> label phone only.
- "Payment on 2023-11-15 for $42.50" -> span: "2023-11-15" -> DATE; span: "$42.50" -> MONEY.
- "user@example.com sent the file" -> span full email -> EMAIL.
sample_annotations: [SAMPLE 1] Text: 'Invoice #A-9931, sent on 04/12/23 to ms.doe@example.com' -> Labels: 'A-9931'=ORDER_ID, '04/12/23'=DATE, 'ms.doe@example.com'=EMAIL
[SAMPLE 2] Text: 'Moved to server 10.0.4.21 at 02:34' -> Labels: none (infra IP), add comment 'infra-ip'
[SAMPLE 4] Text: 'Order: ********1234' -> Labels: '********1234' = PARTIAL_CARD -> mark as PII and uncertain if masked
[SAMPLE 5] Text: 'Error: userId=85f1e2b3-... traceId=9c2' -> Labels: none by default, comment 'likely internal ids'
